title: Process definitions
status: gate met - AC-1..AC-6 met: the steps are listed in their recorded sequence and each names its required role; a cycle in the steps and a cycle between definitions are both displayed with their path; versions are shown with the steps their own snapshots added and removed; the catalogue writes nothing and says so; its instance counts equal WFL-01's for the same field; and the graph is derived from the step list, so it cannot show an edge the steps do not record.

dataModel.decision: Nothing was created. The steps are not a table: PROCESS_DEFINITION.PROCESS_CONFIG_JSON holds the definition, so the catalogue parses it with the owner's own Beep.OilandGas.Models.Processes.ProcessDefinition contract - the same type the engine writes - and reads WORKFLOW_VERSION, WORKFLOW_DEPENDENCY and PROCESS_INSTANCE.
dataModel.openQuestionAnswered: The feature's open question - 'users will ask to edit definitions; a definition editor is out of scope and must be stated in the UI' - is answered by a constant on the catalogue record that the page prints: definitions are code and configuration, so this screen is read-only and no definition is written from here.
dataModel.steps: A definition with no configuration, or one whose configuration does not parse, is shown as invalid with its reason rather than being dropped - the state a person needs when a document is stuck.

rules.ordering: Steps are ordered by their recorded SequenceNumber then by StepId, so the list is the definition's own order rather than the JSON's. Each step's required roles are joined, and a step with none says 'no role recorded'.
rules.decisions: A step's decisions are its recorded StepType, APPROVE/RETURN when it requires an approval, and a NEXT entry per outgoing transition. Its next step keys are the next step plus the conditional next steps, deduplicated.
rules.cycles: Step cycles are found by a depth-first walk of the next-step graph and reported as the path that closes, e.g. S-3 → S-4 → S-3. Dependency cycles are found the same way over WORKFLOW_DEPENDENCY (dependent → prerequisite) and reported separately, so the two kinds are never confused.
rules.versions: A version's difference is computed from its own PROCESS_CONFIG_SNAPSHOT against the snapshot of the version it names as its predecessor: the step ids present in one and not the other. A version with no snapshot says so instead of claiming no change.
rules.scope: Dependencies and versions are read for the opened definition by identity, not by position, and the instance counts use the same field scope WFL-01 applies so the two screens agree.
rules.readOnly: The service opens no unit of work at all, and the page prints the notice - the guard test asserts both.

implementation.service: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Data/Workflow/OgDefinitionCatalogue.cs (OgProcessStep, OgWorkflowDependency, OgWorkflowVersion, OgProcessDefinitionView, OgDefinitionCycle, OgDefinitionCatalogue, DefinitionCatalogueRules, IOgDefinitionCatalogue, OgDefinitionCatalogueService)
implementation.page: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop/Views/DefinitionsPageView.cs (route 'definitions': the field bar, the counts, the read-only notice, the definition grid, the ordered step grid, the graph, the cycles, the version grid and the dependency grid)
implementation.wiring: OgBootstrapper (IOgDefinitionCatalogue), OgApplication.DefinitionCatalogue, catalog 'definitions' (OgModuleKeys.Workflow), OgPageFactory, en + ar labels
implementation.tests: test/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Tests/DefinitionCatalogueTests.cs (7, no database) + DefinitionCatalogueGatewayTests.cs (1 opt-in, real SQLite over six tables)

integration.database: SQLite with PROCESS_DEFINITION, WORKFLOW_VERSION, WORKFLOW_DEPENDENCY, PROCESS_INSTANCE, PROCESS_STEP_INSTANCE and PROCESS_HISTORY. Three definitions: one four-step approval flow whose step 3 points at step 4 and step 4 back at step 3, one three-step flow on another field, and one with no configuration at all; two versions of the first, with snapshots; a two-way dependency between two definitions; three instances.
integration.ac1_steps: the drilling definition lists 4 steps in sequence with 'DrillingEngineer' and 'PeerReviewer, TeamLead' as their roles, an approval step with a 72 hour SLA, and its decisions as ['APPROVAL','APPROVE','RETURN','NEXT:S-3']
integration.sg14_1: the list row reads 'Drilling approval · APPROVAL · version 2.1 · 4 step(s) · 2 instance(s) · active'
integration.ac2_cycles: the opened definition reports the step cycle S-3 → S-4 → S-3, and the definitions that record the dependency report PD-2 → PD-3 → PD-2; the definition with no dependency reports neither
integration.ac3_versions: version 2 reads 'Added the approval step' with added S-4 and no removal, marked superseded; version 1 is its predecessor and the difference comes from the two snapshots
integration.ac4_readonly: PROCESS_DEFINITION and WORKFLOW_VERSION counts are unchanged after the read, and the guard test asserts the service opens no unit of work
integration.ac5_counts: every definition's instance count equals the count WFL-01 reports for the same field, and the catalogue total equals WFL-01's instances in scope
integration.ac6_graph: the graph's nodes are exactly the four step keys and its edges are exactly the four recorded transitions, including S-3 → S-4 and S-4 → S-3
integration.invalid: the definition with no configuration is listed as invalid with 'the definition records no configuration, so it has no steps', and the catalogue counts one invalid
integration.identity: opening PD-2 reads its own (empty) version list rather than the previously selected definition's
integration.failure: dropping WORKFLOW_VERSION fails the read with no catalogue

gates.AC-1 The step list is ordered and names: pass - ordered by SequenceNumber then StepId, roles joined, and a role-less step says so.
gates.AC-2 A cycle in dependencies is displaye: pass - step cycles and dependency cycles are both found and printed with their closing path.
gates.AC-3 Versions are shown with their diffe: pass - added and removed steps computed from consecutive snapshots; a version with no snapshot says so.
gates.AC-4 Definitions are read-only in the de: pass - no unit of work is opened (guard test), the row counts are unchanged, and the page prints the notice.
gates.AC-5 Counts of instances using a definit: pass - the gateway compares every definition's count and the total against WFL-01's dashboard for the same field.
gates.AC-6 The graph matches the step list exa: pass - nodes and edges are projected from the step list itself, so a graph edge cannot exist without a recorded transition.

stepsAreConfigNotATable.finding: There is no PROCESS_DEFINITION_STEP table: the definition's steps live in PROCESS_CONFIG_JSON. The owner already models them as Beep.OilandGas.Models.Processes.ProcessDefinition with ProcessStepDefinition rows.
stepsAreConfigNotATable.handling: The catalogue deserializes PROCESS_CONFIG_JSON into that same owner contract, so the viewer and the engine cannot disagree about what a step is. A configuration that does not parse is reported through the failure reporter and shown as the definition's invalid reason.

guardCaughtAListAdd.finding: The first read-only guard asserted no '.Add(new' in the service and flagged cycles.Add(new OgDefinitionCycle(...)) - a list append, not a database write.
guardCaughtAListAdd.handling: The guard now asserts the write surface that matters: no unit of work is opened, and there is no Update, Commit or Delete call.

liveConfigVersusSnapshot.finding: The gateway first expected the live definition to hold three steps while the schema seeded it with the four-step version, so the diff assertion and the step count disagreed.
liveConfigVersusSnapshot.handling: The scenario now states it plainly: the live configuration is the four-step version and version 1 is the three-step snapshot the difference is measured against.

selectionWasByPosition.finding: The first gateway scenario assumed the first listed definition was the drilling one; the list is ordered by name, so the first row is 'Completion sign-off'.
selectionWasByPosition.handling: The detail is opened by identity (LoadAsync with the definition id) - which is also the rule the stage states: never pick 'the latest' or the positional one, always the exact record.

limits: Definitions cannot be edited: they are code and configuration in the owning project, and the feature explicitly excludes an editor. WFL-06 owns workflow administration.
The dependency cycle is computed over WORKFLOW_DEPENDENCY rows as a directed graph; it does not evaluate CONDITION_EXPRESSION, so a dependency that is conditional is treated as present.
A version's difference compares step ids only: a changed role, SLA or decision on the same step id is not shown as a difference, only an added or removed step.
ROLE_HANDOFF_CONTRACT is not displayed: the handoff rules (required data, documents, approval context) belong to the handoff panels the feature lists for WFL-06.
The graph is a node and edge list rather than a drawn diagram; the stage's shared StepGraph control is not built, and the substitution is stated rather than presented as the control.
The step list is read from the definition's current configuration, so a historical step that a version has since removed is visible only in the version's diff, not in the step grid.
Uses of a definition ('where is this used') are shown as instance counts only; documents that reference a definition are not enumerated, because no table links a document to a definition.
No paging: each read loads the four tables whole and filters in memory.
No per-command permission enforcement beyond the page gate: workflow.read is not checked per read.
